export const meta = {
  name: 'polish-and-bonus',
  description: 'UI polish + create-lease form with live preview (backend options service first), allocation unit tests, then one reviewer',
  phases: [{ title: 'Build' }, { title: 'Review' }],
}
const COMMON = `Timed build lane (feature freeze at 03:48Z). Working dir ./app. Source of truth ../BRIEF.md; ../SPEC.md; ../DECISIONS.md (D1-D63, all decided). The brief overrides CLAUDE.md where SPEC.md says so (error body {error: string}; status computed with invoiceStatus; MYT everywhere). One simple command per Bash call; never npm i; never commit; NEVER run supabase db reset; DB/test commands via bash ../scripts/with-db.sh <cmd>. Dev server runs at :3000 (hot reload; never start/kill it). Edit ONLY your listed files. Keep changes small and safe: tests are green now (1152) and must stay green.`
const S = { type: 'object', properties: { status: { type: 'string' }, files_changed: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, checks_run: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, assumptions: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } }, required: ['status', 'files_changed', 'checks_run', 'assumptions'] }
const R = { type: 'object', properties: { verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['PASS', 'FAIL'] }, findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { severity: { type: 'string' }, file: { type: 'string' }, line: { type: 'string' }, problem: { type: 'string' }, fix: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['severity', 'file', 'problem', 'fix'] } } }, required: ['verdict', 'findings'] }

phase('Build')
const alloc = agent(`${COMMON}
Task: bonus "Unit tests for allocation" (R26, R27, R24). Files you may edit: tests/unit/allocation.test.ts (new). Use tests/helpers (createFixtureOrg, db/newConnection; read tests/helpers/README.md). Exercise private.record_payment / approve_payment / void_payment / allocate_payment through pg as postgres inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK (or on fixture leases), with describe names starting 'R26'. Cover: fill order due_date, deposit before rent on the same day, period_index; each invoice filled up to its unpaid amount before the next; invoices not yet due are filled too; partial fill leaves the next invoice partially paid; a manager payment equal to the whole balance pays everything with unapplied 0; an online payment (create_gateway_bill + apply_gateway_callback) larger than the remaining balance ends with unapplied_sen = the leftover; void deletes only that payment's allocations and other payments' allocations and unapplied_sen are unchanged (D14); a 0-sen rent invoice gets no allocation row; paidSen per invoice = Σ allocations and invoiceStatus over the result matches expectations; allocations never exceed an invoice's amount. Done means: bash ../scripts/with-db.sh npx vitest run tests/unit/allocation.test.ts passes; then the whole tests/unit passes.`,
  { agentType: 'test-engineer', label: 'bonus:allocation-tests', phase: 'Build', schema: S })

const be = await agent(`${COMMON}
Task: backend support for the bonus create-lease form (R46, R56). Files you may edit: src/server/services/leases.ts. Add export async function leaseFormOptions(ctx: ServiceCtx): Promise<{ units: { id: string; name: string }[]; tenants: { id: string; fullName: string; email: string }[] }> — loadCaller, requireMember(['manager']) (others 403), returns the caller org's units and tenants (scoped by org_id), sorted by name. Do not change any existing function. Done means: tsc + eslint clean.`,
  { agentType: 'backend-engineer', label: 'bonus:lease-options', phase: 'Build', schema: S })

const ui = await agent(`${COMMON}
Task: UI polish + bonus create-lease form (R49-R52, R56). Files you may edit: src/app/(app)/leases/new/** (new), src/app/(app)/leases/page.tsx, src/app/(app)/dashboard/**, src/components/staff/**, src/components/tenant/**, src/components/app-shell/**.
1. Bonus: /leases/new (managers only; staff/tenant -> redirect to /leases or show 'Only managers can create leases'). Server component loads leaseFormOptions(ctx) from src/server/services/leases.ts (just added). Client form: unit select, tenant select, start date and end date (<input type="date">, YYYY-MM-DD strings — never new Date(string) in local time), monthly rent and deposit typed in ringgit parsed with parseRinggitToSen (deposit may be empty = 0). LIVE PREVIEW: as inputs change, call generateSchedule from src/lib/billing.ts in the browser (wrap in try/catch; show the thrown message as a helpful inline hint) and render the schedule table (kind, period, due date, amount with formatSen) plus the total. Submit POSTs /api/leases { unitId, tenantId, startDate, endDate, monthlyRentSen, depositSen } -> toast success and router.push('/leases/<id>'); 409 -> toast 'This unit already has a lease that overlaps these dates'; other errors -> toast the API's { error }. Loading state on the button. Add a 'New lease' button on /leases visible to managers.
2. Polish (only what is cheap and safe): every page has a clear heading and an empty state; nav links in the header for staff/manager (Dashboard, Leases) and tenant (My tenancy); dashboard overdue count links to /leases; consistent RM formatting via formatSen; no Date rendering on the server that could differ on the client (R52).
Done means: tsc + eslint clean (show output); curl /leases/new as unauthenticated -> 307; existing tests untouched.`,
  { agentType: 'ui-builder', label: 'polish:ui-builder', phase: 'Build', schema: S })

const a = await alloc
phase('Review')
const files = [...((be && be.files_changed) || []), ...((ui && ui.files_changed) || []), ...((a && a.files_changed) || [])]
const rv = await agent(`${COMMON}\nRead-only review of the polish + bonus changes (uncommitted; git diff HEAD and untracked files): ${files.join(', ')}. Check: manager-only enforcement is server-side (POST /api/leases already enforces; the page must not be the only check), generateSchedule used for the preview exactly as the brief's contract, no local-time date parsing, parseRinggitToSen for amounts, toasts + loading states, no hydration risks, no secret in client code, no 'any', tests actually assert allocation rules. Concrete problems only. PASS or FAIL.`,
  { agentType: 'reviewer', label: 'polish:review', phase: 'Review', schema: R })
return { allocation: a, backend: be, ui, review: rv }

allocation.status:
Done. I added one new file, tests/unit/allocation.test.ts, with 9 tests under 3 describes. The R-numbers come first in each describe name: 'R26 R27 allocation order…', 'R26 online payment … unapplied_sen' and 'R24 R26 D14 void…'. Results: `bash ../scripts/with-db.sh npx vitest run tests/unit/allocation.test.ts` gives 1 file passed, 9 tests passed. All of tests/unit gives 5 files passed, 250 tests passed. Under TZ=UTC, TZ=Asia/Kuala_Lumpur and TZ=America/New_York the file passes 9 of 9 each time. tsc and eslint are clean.

How the tests are set up: one fixture org is created and committed in beforeAll (createFixtureOrg). Everything else runs inside BEGIN … ROLLBACK on a dedicated newConnection(), so no payments or audit rows are left behind: the lease, its invoices (exactly generateSchedule's output), payments, gateway bills and allocations. Payment rows only ever come from private.record_payment, approve_payment, void_payment, create_gateway_bill and apply_gateway_callback. Some scenarios insert the deposit invoice after the rent invoices, so the correct order cannot be an accident of insertion order. Expected SQL errors run inside a savepoint so the test can keep going after them.

What each test proves:
1. Fill order. The deposit is filled before rent due the same day (deposit first even though it was inserted last). Each invoice is filled up to its unpaid amount before the next one starts: 250,000 gives deposit 200,000 and p0 50,000. A second payment of 120,000 tops up p0 by 50,000, then puts 70,000 on p1. The first payment's allocation rows stay byte-identical. invoiceStatus gives partially_paid, then overdue at 00:00 MYT the day after the due date.
2. Partial fill. 200,001 leaves p0 with 1 sen paid. It is partially_paid at 23:59:59.999 MYT on its due date and overdue at 00:00 MYT the next day.
3. Not-yet-due invoices are filled. On 2026-01-05, p1 (due 02-01) is already paid and p2 is untouched.
4. Whole balance. A manager payment equal to the whole balance (500,000) pays every invoice exactly, with one allocation row per invoice and unapplied_sen 0. One more sen is refused with P0422.
5. Staff approval. A staff payment is pending and has no allocations. approve_payment then allocates it by the same rule. Calling private.allocate_payment a second time adds nothing (R28).
6. Online leftover. The bill is 400,000. A 150,000 cash payment lands before the callback. The callback fills every invoice, including p2 which is not yet due, and leaves unapplied_sen at 50,000. A duplicate callback returns 'duplicate' with the same payment id and changes nothing.
7. 0-sen rent invoice. Rent of 10 sen with a 1-day final period rounds to a 0-sen invoice. The online payment passes it while it still has 10 sen in hand. No allocation row is created for it, unapplied_sen is 10, and invoiceStatus says paid.
8. Void (D14), mixed payments. Voiding the cash payment deletes only its rows. The online payment keeps exactly its rows (same ids) and its 50,000 unapplied, which is not re-applied. The reopened invoices are overdue. Voiding the same payment again gives P0409.
9. Void, two manager payments. Voiding one leaves the other's rows untouched. A new payment then fills the reopened deposit first.

After every step, a shared invariant check confirms:
- No invoice has more allocated than its amount.
- No allocation row is 0 sen or less.
- For an approved payment, allocations plus unapplied_sen equal the amount, and unapplied_sen is 0 unless the method is online.
- A payment that is not approved has no allocations.

No contract gap found: every function matches SPEC.md and the migration.
checks_run: bash ../scripts/with-db.sh npx vitest run tests/unit/allocation.test.ts -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 9 passed (9)
bash ../scripts/with-db.sh npx vitest run tests/unit -> Test Files 5 passed (5), Tests 250 passed (250)
bash ../scripts/with-db.sh env TZ=UTC npx vitest run tests/unit/allocation.test.ts -> 9 passed (9)
bash ../scripts/with-db.sh env TZ=Asia/Kuala_Lumpur npx vitest run tests/unit/allocation.test.ts -> 9 passed (9)
bash ../scripts/with-db.sh env TZ=America/New_York npx vitest run tests/unit/allocation.test.ts -> 9 passed (9)
assumptions: Leases and invoices are inserted directly with pg inside the rolled-back transaction, using exactly generateSchedule(lease), the same thing insertLease does. I did not reuse insertLease because it commits through the shared pool, and the payments on top of a committed lease could never be cleaned up (append-only, D29). Only the fixture org itself is committed, which the helpers README allows.

Some scenarios insert the deposit invoice after the rent invoices on purpose, to prove the deposit-before-rent order comes from the ORDER BY and not from insertion order. The returned invoices are still in schedule order.
Manual payments use method 'cash' (no slip) so the allocation tests do not depend on Storage. Slip validation is covered in other lanes.

Two cases in the task have no distinct case in this schema, so I covered them indirectly. Period-index ordering is tested through due dates, because generateSchedule never produces two rent invoices with the same due date. 'Deposit before rent on the same day' is the only real tie, and it is tested.
A 0-sen invoice counts as 'paid' through invoiceStatus (paidSen 0 >= amountSen 0, the R17 rule order). The test asserts this as current behaviour.

backend.status: done. I added `leaseFormOptions(ctx: ServiceCtx): Promise<LeaseFormOptions>` to /home/electronica-care/ezy-prep/exam/app/src/server/services/leases.ts, along with an exported type `LeaseFormOptions = { units: { id: string; name: string }[]; tenants: { id: string; fullName: string; email: string }[] }`. It calls loadCaller, then requireMember(caller, ['manager']), so staff, tenants and non-members get the existing 403. It then runs two Prisma reads in parallel, both filtered by the checked orgId: units sorted by name, then id; tenants sorted by full_name, then id. Tenant rows are mapped to { id, fullName, email }. No existing function changed. No route handler or server action was added because the brief listed only this file. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint . --max-warnings=0` both finished with no output. No tests were run and no new tests were added.
assumptions: Tenants are sorted by full_name, the tenants table's only name column.
Ties on the name are broken by id ascending, so the order is always the same.
Sorting is done by Postgres ORDER BY, which uses the database collation instead of a JS string compare. This is fine for a form picker.
The function takes no input, so there is no zod schema. orgId comes only from the caller's membership.

The UI will call this service through a server action or page that its own lane owns. If an HTTP endpoint (e.g. GET /api/leases/form-options) is needed, it must be added to src/app/api/** in a separate task, because this task allowed editing only leases.ts.

ui.status: Done. The create-lease form and header nav are built, and tsc and eslint are clean. I did not check the authenticated pages in a browser; I only confirmed the unauthenticated redirects with curl. Tests were not re-run, and none of the files I changed are ones the tests import.
checks_run: npx eslint . --max-warnings=0: exit 0, no output (the first run had 2 warnings in staff-nav.tsx; I fixed them and re-ran)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}' http://127.0.0.1:3000/leases/new: 307 to http://127.0.0.1:3000/login (/leases gives the same)
Test suite not re-run. I did not touch src/lib, src/server, src/app/api, tests or the DB, and I ran no DB commands. No grep of tests for the edited components was run before the nav change.
assumptions: To see the screens, log in with the shared seed password (SEED_PASSWORD in .env.local). Use manager@northwind.test for /leases/new and the 'New lease' button, staff@northwind.test for the staff view (no button, and /leases/new shows 'Only managers can create leases'), and aisyah@northwind.test for the tenant view (header shows 'My tenancy').

Header nav: AppHeader is now an async server component that reads the caller's role from the DB (getUserId and loadCaller, not user_metadata). Staff and managers get Dashboard and Leases, tenants get My tenancy, and a lookup failure renders no links. The signature AppHeader({ email }) is unchanged, so the (app) layout, the payments layout and the home page still work. The cost is one extra auth call and two extra DB queries per page render.

StaffNav now renders null, because the header carries the same links and showing both would duplicate them. I kept the component and its `active` prop so lease/[leaseId], dashboard and leases pages still compile. I cannot edit lease/[leaseId]/page.tsx. Whoever owns it can drop the <StaffNav/> import later.

On /leases/new, non-managers who are members see a 'Only managers can create leases' card (no redirect). Tenants are redirected to /tenant, and users with no role go to /. This is UX only: leaseFormOptions and POST /api/leases both check the manager role again.
The schedule preview shows at most 120 rows so a very long lease cannot freeze the page. The count and the total still cover every row, and the footer says 'first 120 shown'.
Only the 409 response gets the fixed overlap message. 404 (unit or tenant not in the org), 400 and others toast the API's own { error } text.

I did not generate an idempotency key for lease creation. SPEC.md D9 makes the key optional and for payments only, and POST /api/leases takes no key. That is where I left the CLAUDE.md rule about keys on payment forms.

Dashboard: the overdue number is now a link to /leases, with an aria-label so screen readers hear 'N overdue invoices, view leases'. The data-testid='overdue-count' element keeps the plain number as its text.

R52 needed no change. Every date on staff pages renders from its YYYY-MM-DD string, and tenant instants go through formatMytDisplay (fixed +08:00). The tenant portal sets 'now' only after mount, so server and client output match.
No new packages are needed.

findings.problem: The new service function leaseFormOptions has no test. Nothing checks that it is manager-only (staff and tenant should get 403) or that it returns only the caller's own org's units and tenants. The page check is UX only, so this function is the real gate for the picker data.
findings.fix: Add a test in tests/authz that calls leaseFormOptions with a ctx built from a seeded user. Staff and tenant should get a 403 AppError. The manager should get only own-org unit and tenant ids, with no id from a second fixture org.

findings.problem: After a successful POST, `finally { setSubmitting(false) }` turns the Create button back on while router.push is still navigating. A second click sends another POST. The DB EXCLUDE constraint rejects it, so no data is corrupted, but the user sees the overlap 409 toast for a lease that was just created.
findings.fix: Set submitting back to false only on the error paths, and leave it true after toast.success and router.push.

findings.problem: The preview shows generateSchedule's own error text to the user. For example, a rent of "0" shows "monthlyRentSen must be a positive integer", and reversed dates show "endDate is before startDate". These are developer messages, not UI copy.
findings.fix: Before calling generateSchedule, check monthlyRentSen > 0 and endDate >= startDate (plain string comparison works for valid ISO dates) and show friendly messages. Keep the generic message as the fallback.

findings.problem: The page awaits leaseFormOptions at the top level and the route has no loading.tsx or Suspense boundary. While units and tenants load, the user sees no loading state, even though the brief asks for loading states.
findings.fix: Add src/app/(app)/leases/new/loading.tsx with a form skeleton, or put the options fetch and NewLeaseForm inside a Suspense boundary with a fallback.

findings.problem: StaffNav is now dead code: it always returns null and uses `void props` to silence the unused-parameter warning. Three pages still import it (dashboard, leases, leases/[leaseId]).
findings.fix: Delete staff-nav.tsx and remove the <StaffNav .../> imports and calls from the three pages.
